label: John Milton, Paradise Lost (1667; 2nd ed. 1674)
text: The first of the three books the Creature finds. He later reads Adam's and Satan's stories against his own; the novel's epigraph comes from Book X.

label: Plutarch, Parallel Lives (c. 100 CE)
text: Paired biographies of Greek and Roman statesmen; for the Creature, a first lesson in public virtue.

label: Goethe, The Sorrows of Young Werther (1774)
text: Goethe's novel in letters. The spelling “Werter” is that of the early English versions; the first (1779) was translated from the French.

loc.exact: Like one who, on a lonely road

label: S. T. Coleridge, The Rime of the Ancient Mariner (1798)
text: Quoted without attribution in 1818; the 1831 text adds a footnote naming Coleridge.

label: William Wordsworth, “Lines written a few miles above Tintern Abbey” (1798)
text: Victor applies Wordsworth's lines on his younger self to Clerval.

loc.exact: We rest; a dream has power to poison sleep

label: Percy Bysshe Shelley, “Mutability” (1816)
text: Unattributed in 1818. The Blackwood's reviewer quoted these lines as the author's own verse.

see.exact: We rest; a dream has power to poison sleep.

loc.exact: the affair of the Rue Morgue

label: Edgar Allan Poe, “The Murders in the Rue Morgue” (1841)
text: Dupin's first case, in which the narrator first lodged with him. The Prefect who now comes to consult them is the official Dupin outwitted there, “somewhat too cunning to be profound.”

see.exact: our friend the Prefect is somewhat too cunning to be profound

loc.exact: You remind me of Edgar Allen Poe’s Dupin

label: Edgar Allan Poe, “The Murders in the Rue Morgue” (1841)
text: Watson spells the name “Allen.” The “trick” Holmes mocks next, breaking in on a friend's thoughts after a quarter of an hour's silence, is the walk in the Rue Morgue where Dupin answers the narrator's unspoken thought about the actor Chantilly.

see.exact: neither of us had spoken a syllable for fifteen minutes at least

loc.exact: the dark incidents of the Study in Scarlet

label: Arthur Conan Doyle, A Study in Scarlet (1887)
text: The first case Watson recorded, begun when he and Holmes took rooms together in Baker Street. Holmes there names the case himself: “a study in scarlet, eh?”

loc.exact: Oh, Sherlock Holmes by all means.

label: Arthur Conan Doyle, A Study in Scarlet (1887)
text: Holmes's first case, where he calls himself a consulting detective, the one the government detectives come to when they are at fault. Cynthia's choice, “Scotland Yard? Or Sherlock Holmes?”, is his own.

see.exact: I’m a consulting detective, if you can understand what that is

loc.exact: I could well remember the scorn which the theories of the reasoner used then to excite in the practical man.

label: Arthur Conan Doyle, A Study in Scarlet (1887)
text: Lestrade's earliest appearance beside Holmes in the library. He and Gregson watch Holmes measure the room “with considerable curiosity and some contempt”, and Lestrade tells him that “the old hound is the best, when all is said and done.”

see.exact: Gregson and Lestrade had watched the manœuvres of their amateur companion with considerable curiosity and some contempt.

loc.exact: the terrible “Moby Dick” of hyperborean regions

label: Herman Melville, Moby-Dick (1851)
text: Melville's white whale, set here among the kraken and the sea-serpent as a fable of sailors.
